original_question: Can one define a notion of dimension for a useful class of fields F such that Br.dim(F) <= dim F - 1 and dim(F(t)) = dim F + 1?
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual target: it correctly identifies that the question is about defining a field-theoretic notion of dimension tied to Brauer dimension, and it reproduces the two desiderata involving Br.dim(F) and the one-variable rational function field F(t). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
missing_details: The paper's notation Br.dim(F) needs to be defined explicitly: in Section 4 it is the least integer d such that ind(A) divides per(A)^d for every central simple F-algebra A; if no such d exists, Br.dim(F)=∞. Your draft uses Br.dim(F) without supplying this definition. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))

The paper asks for a notion of dimension on some class of fields, not necessarily on all fields. For a stand-alone formulation, the class should at least be understood to contain both F and F(t) whenever the second axiom is invoked; the paragraph immediately before Problem 4.5 explicitly motivates restricting attention to certain fields. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
t should be specified as an indeterminate, so that F(t) means the rational function field in one variable over F. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
The sought dimension should be stated as numerical/integer-valued; this is implicit in the displayed axioms but not explicit in your draft. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))

The paper is using its global Brauer-dimension notion here, not the prime-specific Brauer p-dimension introduced just above. A stand-alone question should avoid that ambiguity. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))

Nearby context that sharpens intent is missing from the draft: the authors immediately suggest, only as one possible normalization, that one might declare dim(F)=Br.dim(F)+1, and they explicitly say that cohomological dimension is not the right notion because of Merkurjev's example. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
refined_question: Can one define an integer-valued notion dim on some class of fields, closed under adjoining one transcendental indeterminate t, such that for every field F in that class one has Br.dim(F) ≤ dim(F)-1 and dim(F(t)) = dim(F)+1, where Br.dim(F) denotes the smallest integer d for which ind(A) divides per(A)^d for every central simple F-algebra A, and Br.dim(F)=∞ if no such d exists? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation to your draft: Section 4, Problem 4.5 asks exactly for a notion of field-dimension satisfying the two displayed properties you quoted, and the surrounding discussion supplies the needed notation and scope. The opening of Section 4 defines Brauer dimension; the paragraph just before Problem 4.5 explains that the authors have in mind restricting to particular classes of fields; and the sentence immediately after Problem 4.5 gives only a possible normalization, not a proved equivalent reformulation. So your draft is substantively correct but not fully stand-alone until Br.dim(F), the meaning of F(t), and the scope "some class of fields" are made explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1006.3304))
